newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ National list MP Gerard accepts Canadian post.
newsitem.headline: NZ National list MP Gerard accepts Canadian post.

text.p: National list MP Jim Gerard has accepted a post as High Commissioner to Canada after being passed over as National's candidate for the position of Speaker of Parliament, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Monday.
Gerard issued a statement saying he had informed Foreign Affairs Minister Don McKinnon he would accept the post.
"I have discussed the offer with my family and the Canterbury/Westland division of the National Party and have their full support.
"I consider it an honour to be able to represent my country, and look forward to the challenge," Gerard said.

The National-New Zealand First Government last week installed Kaikoura MP and former ACC and Fisheries Minister Doug Kidd as Speaker, clearing a space in cabinet for new MPs from NZ First and National's back benches.
The move was bitterly opposed by Labour, who had been willing to support Gerard -- who has served as deputy speaker for the past two parliamentary terms -- as Speaker.

Labour MP Mike Moore, who defeated Gerard in the Waimakariri seat at this year's election, said installing Kidd at Gerard's expense was a "dirty double-crossing deal" which had "nothing to do with ability".
Gerard's statement did not say when he was due to take up his new posting. The current High Commissioner, former National cabinet minister Maurice McTigue, is due to end his three-year term in April.
Gerard's decision means his place in Parliament will go to the next person on National's party list, Wellington lawyer Annabel Young.
